A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TrajViT work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary Sections 6–13 support reliable comparison despite reference relocation and repagination.

before.justification: V2 reports original retrieval, classification, detection, VideoQA, scaling and ablation results, including supplementary image-only experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experimental results in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: The trajectory extraction pipeline, appearance and position encoding, transformer architecture, contrastive training and image integration remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same Panda70M and DataComp training coverage and video retrieval, classification, detection, clip retrieval, VideoQA and image-only evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including ViT3D, TokenLearner, ViViT, AutoMerge, RLT and ToMe. The VideoLLM, image-only and ablation comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: The training subsets, frame sampling, model sizes, budgets and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. This includes ViT-Large main experiments and ViT-Base ablations on 880k videos.

E4.justification: Tables 5–6 retain the same segmentation/tracking, pipeline and encoder ablations. Scaling analyses and supplementary trajectory examples, including matching failures, are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and 9–12 and Figures 6–9 retain the same numerical results and trends. For example, Table 4's NextQA open-ended scores remain 49.2 for ViT3D and 65.1 for TrajViT. Supplementary qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (1), its mathematical definitions and the trajectory formulation are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same novelty, token-reduction and accuracy/efficiency claims. The shortened conclusion preserves their scientific meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations and limitations concerning SSV2 overcompression, tracking overhead, trajectory matching failures and weaker image-only performance.

D1.justification: V3 removes the first-page project URL and the explicit code-availability statement with its repository link, without replacement elsewhere. Implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and all 75 cited works are retained. Bibliographic spelling, hyphenation and placement differences do not change the cited research.

P1.justification: V3 shortens the conclusion, adds a Toyota funding acknowledgement and corrects 'table ??' to Table 8 in Section 7. References move after the supplementary text; the remaining prose is essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 6–9 are re-embedded as raster graphics with altered text rendering but unchanged plots. Repagination brings the conclusion onto page 8 and interleaves the bibliography with retained Figures 11–12; table structures and other illustrations remain intact.

improvement.justification: V3 preserves the scientific evidence but removes both project and code access links, reducing the paper's support for locating the implementation. The corrected Table 8 reference and added funding disclosure are modest benefits that do not offset this limited loss of reproducibility information.
